newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares seek to break out of range trade.
newsitem.headline: German shares seek to break out of range trade.

text.p: German shares on Tuesday sought to break out of lacklustre range trade as limited volumes kept the market relatively steady despite the dollar maintaining its gains and an overnight Wall Street advance.
The IBIS DAX, which reflects all-day trading, was up 10.60 points at 3,383.56 points at 0800 GMT. The 30-share DAX index ended bourse trade on Monday down 14.21 points at 3,363.06.
"Despite the relatively friendly influence from Wall Street, the German market is rather sluggish," SuedwestLB said in its morning market commentary.
Traders looked for the DAX index to remain within a range from 3,360 to 3,400 points for the session and also possibly on Wednesday ahead of Thursday's market holiday.

But some said the DAX could break the psychologically important 3,400 level during the week and keep up the advance led by dollar-sensitive shares, particularly carmakers, if volumes were to return to the market.
"A lot will depend on when institutional investors return to the market and we can shake off this lethargic feeling," said one trader, noting the lack of fresh market orders.
Among specific shares, ball-bearings maker Kugelfischer was one of the top percentage gainers, rising 60 pfennigs to 31.10 marks after reporting higher 1996 profits.
Industrial group Daimler-Benz was up 30 pfennigs at 127.80 marks ahead of its public introduction today in Frankfurt of its new A-class compact vehicle.
Chemicals group Degussa fell 50 pfennigs to 79.50 marks despite reporting a 25 percent gain in first half profits and giving an optimistic outlook for the second half.
